title: file_picker
objectives: Understand file_picker via a real-life analogy
Pick files across mobile / desktop / Web with correct API
Filter by extension + type; multi-select + drag-and-drop
Handle iOS Files app + Android Storage Access Framework quirks
Save files via file save dialog on desktop

sections.markdown:
**Think of `file_picker` as the system 'Open File' dialog wired to Flutter.**

Where `image_picker` opens the OS photo picker, `file_picker` opens the OS file picker — SAF (Storage Access Framework) on Android, `UIDocumentPicker` on iOS, native file dialogs on desktop, `<input type="file">` on Web.

- **Any file** — you don't need to know the extension; `FileType.any` accepts everything.
- **Filtered** — `FileType.custom` + `allowedExtensions: ['pdf', 'docx', 'csv']`.
- **Media** — `FileType.image` / `.video` / `.audio` shortcuts.
- **Multi-select** — `allowMultiple: true`.
- **Path vs bytes** — mobile returns a real filesystem path; Web returns bytes (no filesystem).
- **Save dialog (desktop)** — `saveFile()` prompts for target location.

**Why every 'attach a document' Flutter app installs it:** system pickers give users familiar UX + cross-app integrations (Google Drive, iCloud, Dropbox all show up in the picker). Building a native browser is a multi-week job — this delegates entirely.

**`file_picker`** wraps: Android **Storage Access Framework** (SAF) via `ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT`, iOS **UIDocumentPickerViewController**, macOS/Windows/Linux **native file dialogs**, Web `<input type="file">`. Also supports **drag-and-drop** on desktop (via `desktop_drop` under the hood on some versions). API: `FilePicker.platform.pickFiles(...)`, `getDirectoryPath()`, `saveFile()`. Returns `FilePickerResult` with `List<PlatformFile>` (name, path, bytes on Web, size, extension).

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Assuming `path` is always non-null.** On Web, `path` is null; use `bytes`. On mobile, path is the norm. Feature-detect via `kIsWeb`.
**Mistake 2: Not calling `withData: true` when needed.** By default on mobile, `bytes` is null (only path). For upload where you need in-memory bytes, request them.
**Mistake 3: Big files loaded via `withData: true`.** A 100 MB video becomes a huge byte array in RAM — OOM. Stream from path instead.
**Mistake 4: Ignoring temp-file cleanup on Android SAF.** SAF caches picked files under the app's temp dir; `clearTemporaryFiles()` after use.
**Mistake 5: Long-lived file references.** Android SAF may revoke the URI after some time / device reboot. If you need durable access, copy the file into your app's own storage.
**Mistake 6: Assuming iOS 'copy' semantics.** On iOS, files from iCloud Drive may be lazily downloaded; access can throw if not-yet-cached. Use `NSFileCoordinator` semantics via the plugin.
**Mistake 7: Multi-select with too many files.** UI thread blocked while paths + metadata come back. Consider batching.
**Mistake 8: Assuming user cancel throws.** Cancel returns null; guard `result == null`.
## Best practices
**1. Feature-detect Web** — use `bytes`; on mobile use `path`.
**2. Filter by extension** for better UX.
**3. Only `withData` when needed** — stream from path for large files.
**4. Copy to app storage** if you need durable access.
**5. `clearTemporaryFiles` after upload.**
**6. Progress indicator** for uploads.
**7. `saveFile` on desktop** for export flows.
**8. Consider `file_selector`** (Flutter team) — simpler; less feature-full — alternative.
## Practice programs

## Interview Q&A

**Q1: file_picker vs image_picker — when each?**

**A:** **`image_picker`** — photos + videos ONLY, uses the OS PHOTO picker (iOS PHPickerViewController + Android Photo Picker). Very compact API. Best for profile pictures, chat photo attach. **`file_picker`** — any file type; uses the OS FILE picker (SAF / UIDocumentPicker / native file dialogs / <input type=file>). Best for: PDF / DOC / spreadsheet uploads, ZIP imports, generic 'attach a document' flows. **Also file_picker handles directory + save dialogs**; image_picker doesn't. **Rule:** photo → image_picker (better UX, no library permission); document → file_picker (universal). Some apps use both: `image_picker` for photo path; `file_picker` for the doc path.

**Q2: How do you handle Web + desktop + mobile with one code path?**

**A:** The tricky bit is `PlatformFile.path` vs `bytes`. On mobile + desktop, `path` is a real file path — cheap to access, stream-friendly. On Web, `path` is null — only `bytes` is populated (unless you set `withData: false`, in which case you get nothing). **Pattern:** feature-detect. Upload via Dio:

```dart
final mpf = kIsWeb
  ? MultipartFile.fromBytes(f.bytes!, filename: f.name)
  : await MultipartFile.fromFile(f.path!, filename: f.name);
```

**For 100 MB files:** don't request `withData` on mobile — path suffices, and streaming avoids OOM. On Web, big files can crash the tab — set a size limit + warn users. **Directory picking** works on desktop + Android SAF; not iOS or Web. Feature-gate the button.

**Q3: What's the Android Storage Access Framework quirk?**

**A:** Android SAF returns a URI (not a file path in the classic sense), pointing to a file that lives in **another app's storage** — Google Drive, Downloads, Files by Google. The plugin copies the file into your app's temporary cache + gives you a real path — but that path is TEMPORARY. **Consequences:** (1) Ephemeral — Android may clear the cache; if you need persistent access, copy to `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()` immediately. (2) Doesn't survive reboot — URIs are session-scoped unless you took a persistable-URI permission (rare from Flutter). (3) `clearTemporaryFiles()` cleans up post-upload. **iOS analog:** UIDocumentPickerViewController returns files from iCloud / Files app; may lazily download; use security-scoped bookmarks for long-term access (usually plugin-transparent).

**Q4: How do you handle very large files (100 MB+)?**

**A:** **Don't request `withData: true`** — that loads the whole file into memory. Use `path` + stream. **For Dio uploads:** `MultipartFile.fromFile(path)` streams from disk. **For processing:** use `File(path).openRead()` for a `Stream<List<int>>` you can chunk. **On Web:** large files crash tabs; set a client-side limit + warn ('files >100 MB not supported on Web; use the desktop app'). **UX:** show a progress bar (Dio's `onSendProgress`); allow cancel via `CancelToken`. **Server:** chunked upload with resumable protocol (tus.io, S3 multipart) for reliability on flaky networks. Interviewers respect the streaming + resumable-upload answer.

**Q5: `file_picker` vs `file_selector` — what's the difference?**

**A:** **`file_selector`** is the Flutter team's official minimal package — smaller API surface, cleaner cross-platform semantics, but limited features (no drag-drop, no directory pick on some platforms). **`file_picker`** is community — more features (media type filters, `withData`, `clearTemporaryFiles`, `getDirectoryPath` on more platforms) but occasional platform quirks. **When to pick each:** `file_selector` for simple 'open a file' needs + adherence to Flutter team maintenance; `file_picker` for feature-rich flows (multi-select, filters, directories). **Migration low friction** — both use `XFile`-like return types. Interviewer bonus: knowing both packages + preferring based on scope.

**Q6: What are common security + privacy concerns?**

**A:** **(1) Malicious files.** Users may upload malware / EXE. Scan server-side; don't execute; validate MIME + magic bytes; ClamAV or a commercial scanner. **(2) File type spoofing.** Extension `.pdf` ≠ actual PDF; sniff magic bytes. **(3) Path traversal (server-side).** Never trust filenames verbatim; sanitize or use UUIDs. **(4) Excessive size.** Enforce client + server limits. **(5) EXIF / metadata leaks.** Documents / photos may embed PII; strip on server or warn user. **(6) `withData` for huge files leaks memory.** **(7) Cache leaks.** SAF temp files linger; `clearTemporaryFiles`. **(8) Sharing across apps** — on Android, granting URI access to your app persists; revoke when done. **(9) DLP (Data Loss Prevention)** on enterprise MDM devices may block file access entirely — handle gracefully.

## Real-world usage

- **Document upload** — chat, email, form attachments.
- **Import / export** — CSV import for a stock app; JSON export.
- **Backup/restore** — pick backup file.
- **Data migration** — importing from another app's export.
- **NOT ideal for** — pure photo flows (image_picker better); background file scanning.

## Advanced notes

- **`FilePickerResult.count`** — number of selected files.
- **`PlatformFile.readStream`** — chunk-reading option for streaming ingest.
- **`dialogTitle`** — set the picker dialog title.
- **`initialDirectory`** — starting folder (desktop / Web).
- **`lockParentWindow`** — desktop modal parent.
- **`onFileLoading`** callback — progress on Web.
- **`file_picker_pro`** — commercial fork with additional features (rare).
- **Drag-and-drop** — use `desktop_drop` package separately for stronger DnD; `file_picker` has limited support.
- **`readAsBytesSync` gotcha** — not available on Web; use `readStream` or `bytes` accessor.
- **iOS UIDocumentPicker mode** — `import` vs `open` semantics differ; plugin normalizes.
- **`saveFile` on Web** — no native save dialog; download bytes via anchor click.
- **File association (desktop)** — configure the app's supported file types in `Info.plist` / manifest for OS-level 'Open with' integration.
